item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports exploring textual–collaborative fusion, but this search found no verified 2024–2026 method satisfying all constraints: sequential recommendation, scratch-trained text encoding, uncertainty gating, and no external weights. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines titles, descriptions and reviews with BERT-based representations; its largest reported textual gains come from reviews, making those results unsuitable evidence for this titles/descriptions-only setting. [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) addresses textual–collaborative imbalance through quantized semantic codes and cross-attention; its abstract does not establish a scratch-only encoder. These findings motivate testing fusion, without establishing gains under the benchmark’s restrictions.\n\nA lightweight admissible experiment: randomly initialized word/subword embeddings, masked mean pooling of titles and truncated descriptions, and a small projection trained jointly with SASRec’s next-item objective. [fastText’s official implementation](https://github.com/facebookresearch/fastText) provides precedent for efficient locally trained word/subword representations, though not evidence for sequential-ranking improvements. Proposed evidence-aware fusion: a conservative residual gate conditioned on training interaction counts, history length and text availability; force the text contribution to zero for missing text. Treat counts as evidence proxies, not calibrated uncertainty. Compare behavior-only SASRec, text-only, fixed fusion and learned gating; report common macro validation HR@10 plus sparse-item and missing-text diagnostics. Titles may encode specifications, but cannot establish ownership, compatibility or unmet needs. These architectural and diagnostic choices are hypotheses to validate, not published results demonstrated by the sources above."}
